scope: Observable contracts and implementation ownership. Contract-tested reports only this foundation; no native worker acceptance is claimed.

scenarios.name: Strict CLI and JSON shape
scenarios.oracle: Invalid flags, duplicate keys, missing fields and unknown versions return nonzero without any record or Git write. JSON record validation is tested here; workspace CLI is pending.

scenarios.name: Immutable run base
scenarios.oracle: Capture the configured commit from registered rig scope, move caller HEAD, and prove the same run still resolves the captured base. Conflicting replay leaves its record unchanged.

scenarios.name: Explicit ordered source plan
scenarios.oracle: Accept one explicit acyclic ordered graph and refuse missing edges, duplicate members, cycles, unreachable terminal and implicit fan-in. Shape/count constraints are tested here; graph traversal is pending.

scenarios.name: Layout and unrelated caller CWD

implementation_owner.component: Workspace adapter / native mode and placement

scenarios.oracle: In ordinary, bare-root and bare-.git fixtures, prepare each permitted parent layout from an unrelated CWD. Verify exact common Git dir, owner, physical record, native attempt and input; refuse foreign checkout ancestors.

scenarios.name: Isolated accepted outputs
scenarios.oracle: Two members start at one captured base in distinct owned workspaces; project checks and independent review bind their exact outputs. Completion alone and unrelated commits cannot supply accepted output.

scenarios.name: Dependent exact input
scenarios.oracle: Keep the dependent blocked until the predecessor has an accepted output; then launch at that exact OID. Refuse default-branch input, premature close/readiness and a semantically reverted prerequisite.

scenarios.name: Shared-chain checkpoints

implementation_owner.component: Shared owner / concrete final source step

scenarios.oracle: Use one stable owner and provisioning attempt through ordered members, with changed and no-change results. Each exact accepted result advances once; stale member/retry cannot advance or rewrite it.

scenarios.name: Ordered integration
scenarios.oracle: Integrate explicit predecessor outputs in recorded order; preserve both independent A/B behaviors and record one tested/reviewed output. Refuse missing, reordered or unaccepted inputs.

scenarios.name: Preserved conflict recovery
scenarios.oracle: Induce a real merge conflict, retain files and operation state, emit an open blocker, and let explicit recovery record a matching decision before result. Unknown state receives no repair or result.

scenarios.name: Known partial replay

implementation_owner.component: Workspace recovery / shared and canonical writers

scenarios.oracle: Fault between member result and owner advance, owner output and canonical pointer, and resolved blocker and phase restore. Exact retry fills only missing state; conflicting state remains unchanged.

scenarios.name: Unknown state refusal
scenarios.oracle: Wrong path, repository registration, owner, attempt, OID, active member, dirty state, mode or Git operation yields a blocker and preserves existing work. Native ancestry and exact member input are checked separately.

scenarios.name: Canonical terminal binding
scenarios.oracle: Bind only the source plan terminal accepted output, member-result digest and exact summary digest. Reject a different OID, nonterminal owner, changed summary or conflicting pointer.

scenarios.name: Exact review and fix invalidation
scenarios.oracle: Review detached exact canonical source with before/after HEAD and dirty-state checks. A fix generation consumes reviewed OID, preserves evidence and invalidates old approval; self-review does not authorize output.

scenarios.name: Source-bound publication
scenarios.oracle: Authorized publication consumes the exact approved OID and hashes. Stale/different source refuses effects; lost remote response becomes uncertain until observed remote OID is reconciled.

scenarios.name: Exact continuations
scenarios.oracle: Resume convoy, decomposition, plan, requirements, review, fix and publish from existing root/generation/records and artifact digests. Never recapture ambient base; missing legacy identity blocks with migration evidence.

scenarios.name: Native end-to-end paths
scenarios.oracle: Run separate, dependent, shared, fanout/fanin, review-fix, publish and restart paths on one pinned core/pack/fixture tuple with actual native workers. Assert prerequisite behavior survives downstream output and record every acceptance result.

scenarios.name: Public layout propagation
scenarios.oracle: Pass nondefault layout variables through every public build, implementation and continuation entrypoint; compare recorded/native layout from unrelated CWD and immutable run rig root despite mutable gc.work_dir.

scenarios.name: Closed current source manifest
scenarios.oracle: Discover all formulas and workflow assets in the five packs, match explicit classifications and content hashes, and verify concrete final-source steps plus direct delegation bindings. Unlisted or changed paths fail the contract tests.

scenarios.name: Legacy migration and refusal
scenarios.oracle: Separate cases: an explicit legacy run completes entirely in legacy mode, and an unclassified shadowed asset refuses with migration evidence. Mixed lifecycle paths and implicit adoption earn no success.

scenarios.name: Dedicated-record concurrency
scenarios.oracle: Use a nondispatched dedicated record that runtime does not update. Race cooperating distinct-key writes with deterministic barriers and real-store stress, with/without the owner lock; bind backend and conditional-write capabilities. Isolation/filter proof is separate from a bead type.

scenarios.name: Scoped lock contention
scenarios.oracle: Race independent root/generation/owner scopes and common-Git registration; prove isolated owner progress, fixed owner-before-root ordering, no deadlock and a bounded lock-timeout blocker. Process timeout is unknown completion.

scenarios.name: Exact writer and filesystem admission
scenarios.oracle: Read back native claim and bind exact writer step/attempt, root/generation/stable owner and active member. Refuse absent/stale bindings, assignee-only evidence and unsupported filesystem locks; demonstrate dedicated records cannot be dispatched.

scenarios.name: Malformed and stale record refusal
scenarios.oracle: Every kind refuses missing required fields, unknown versions, duplicate keys and conflicting root/generation replay. Record validation is tested here; runtime resume must preserve state and emit the corresponding blocker.

rfc_differences.reason: RFC logical identities and lock filenames can collide when an owner/source anchor is reused by another run or generation.
rfc_differences.contract: Every logical identity includes workflow_root_id and generation. Owner lock scope is (common_git_dir, workflow_root_id, generation, workspace_owner_id); root lock scope includes root/generation. Version is validated before lookup.

rfc_differences.reason: RFC dotted physical record names are a naming proposal, not a required storage capability.
rfc_differences.contract: Native-generated physical Beads IDs are returned by explicit kind/full-identity lookup. Missing or multiple references refuse; no record ID is synthesized from owner names.

rfc_differences.reason: Assignment does not prove a current native claim, and the current writer is not the stable workspace owner or native provisioning attempt.
rfc_differences.contract: Claim binding includes exact writer_step_id and writer_attempt_id with root/generation/owner. Writers must read back current claim/ownership under the selected lock; assignee alone never authorizes a write.

rfc_differences.reason: A dedicated milestone or task type is not intrinsically excluded from native ready/dispatch selection.
rfc_differences.contract: Lifecycle record storage must prove a nondispatch status/configuration/filter and exclusion from runtime metadata writers. Backend qualification owns that fixture; schemas alone supply no dispatch isolation.

rfc_differences.reason: Current native launch reconstructs managed ownership from the invoking work bead; literal detached worktrees and default nested placement also need shared native support.
rfc_differences.contract: Stable workspace owner and physical workspace record stay separate from invoking step. Native provenance is opaque and immutable for its provisioning attempt. work_branch may be null to represent detached mode; launch/mode/placement support is a separate bounded native extension.

rfc_differences.reason: Shared members advance source input while native provisioning base describes the initial workspace creation.
rfc_differences.contract: Never rewrite native base_ref/base_sha per checkpoint. Member input/current/output OIDs own progression; native_attempt_id and writer_attempt_id remain distinct.

rfc_differences.reason: RFC blanket no-CAS and whole-column-loss claims describe older implementations and cannot qualify a selected current backend.
rfc_differences.contract: Record schemas remain backend-independent. Selected store/binary must prove conditional-write, patch, claim and isolation capabilities before runtime adoption; unsupported external CAS fails closed.

rfc_differences.reason: Current do-work preparation resolves/fetches the remote default rather than only reading ambient HEAD, and newer drain-wrapper source-anchor resolution exists.
rfc_differences.contract: Migration captures a configured/default commit once from registered rig scope, replaces caller-CWD placement, and preserves current root-stamped and synthetic-wrapper source-anchor handling.

rfc_differences.reason: Current gstack-work reads source-anchor work_dir and explicitly commits; gstack-work-item has its own concrete implement-item override.
rfc_differences.contract: Both gstack leaf assets require path and final-result migration. The manifest binds the concrete implement/implement-item assets rather than declaring no path migration or relying only on inheritance.

rfc_differences.reason: Current BMAD implement-story and apply-story-findings already resolve root-stamped/synthetic source anchors and commit changes.
rfc_differences.contract: Preserve that resolution and checkpoint after the story loop final possible source edit, apply-story-findings. Superpowers checkpoints at record-item-result after its review/fix expansion.

rfc_differences.reason: Base, Compound and gstack shared-item assets have no explicit focused commit-creation instruction.
rfc_differences.contract: Their concrete final source step is recorded with missing-explicit-commit. Migration must supply its accepted output/checkpoint contract; this foundation does not claim an existing commit guarantee.

rfc_differences.reason: The closed inventory includes planning and artifact-only assets beyond the RFC migration surface.
rfc_differences.contract: reference marks explicitly inventoried non-lifecycle surfaces; legacy marks current lifecycle responsibilities. Missing or changed inventory entries fail. Classification is source discovery, not launch admission or migration completion.

rfc_differences.reason: RFC member completion fields alone do not bind project acceptance to exact source.
rfc_differences.contract: Accepted member output carries exact-OID project checks and an independent review report plus artifact hashes. Structural validation cannot verify Git ancestry, artifact bytes, reviewer identity or actual acceptance execution.
